task: Retire closed-loop worker lifecycle controls and standalone group reads from the quote page while preserving UI-owned page refresh
decision: The quote page no longer displays or controls review/broadcast worker lifecycle. ReviewSupervisor, BroadcastSupervisor, and the native worker pool own threads, queues, and heartbeat; M6/M7 managers own durable state and terminal outcomes. The page reads closed-loop groups from the manager-owned /api/dex/quote-routes projection and keeps its own browser-side refresh timer. The timer may temporarily use the current worker interval as its default, but it only re-reads manager data and never starts, stops, or reschedules workers.
changes: Removed worker cards, worker status/next/meta rendering functions, latestRustWorkers state, and worker-only template styles from the quote page
Removed closed-loop group and loop-family start/stop/refresh data attributes, event handlers, and UI rendering paths
Removed the quote page's standalone /api/dex/closed-loop-groups read and now render closedLoopGroups from the manager-only /api/dex/quote-routes payload
Preserved per-route manual review as a command ingress to ReviewSupervisor; backend busy responses remain structured instead of being inferred from a UI worker snapshot
Preserved the UI-owned refreshInterval, localStorage persistence, scheduleRefresh(), and setInterval(refreshSnapshot, seconds * 1000) page timer
Added UI guards that reject worker lifecycle controls and standalone group reads while requiring the manager quote-routes read path and browser refresh ownership
Documented that page refresh cadence can temporarily reuse the worker interval as a default but must later become an independent page parameter
Documented that group-level start/stop/refresh server routes remain maintenance and diagnostic entry points, not page controls

knownBoundary: D9.19 removes worker lifecycle controls and standalone group reads from the quote page. It does not remove maintenance/diagnostic group start/stop/refresh routes, migrate per-route manual review to a manager command API, apply production manager data, start or stop the service, write the mainnet database, or enable real broadcast. The current 60-second page default may reuse the current worker interval, but it is not a worker control and should later become an independent page setting. No historical evidence was modified.
